anomalies.observed: On the EthernetAndPower sheet the RJ45 transformer winding pins are wired to the wrong nets: TD+->LAN1_TX+, TCT->LAN1_TX-, TD->LAN1_RX+, RCT->LAN1_RX-, RD+->LED0, and RD- left unconnected (no-connect). The LED0 global net is the same net that on the SkylabModule sheet drives U5.31 (P4_LED) and the Q2 gate (the EPD high-side power-switch control). Thus a GPIO/switch-control net is merged onto an Ethernet data-winding pin, the differential pairs are tied into the transformer center taps (TCT/RCT), and the receive pair is broken (RD- open).
anomalies.expected: The specification's open item states that in the reference design 'the RJ45 jack J5's data pads (TD+/TD-/RD+/RD-, center-taps, shield) all appear in the netlist as individually unconnected ... while the LAN1_RX+/-, LAN1_TX+/- global labels ... resolve to single-node nets containing only U5 pins.' Even if J5 is meant to be wired, sound practice requires TD+/TD -> the TX differential pair, RD+/RD -> the RX differential pair, the center taps (TCT/RCT) to the PHY common, and the link/activity LED0 GPIO to one of the jack's LED pins (L1-L4) - never to a data-winding pin, and never merging the display-power-switch net with an Ethernet line.

evidence.quote: the RJ45 jack J5's data pads (TD+/TD-/RD+/RD-, center-taps, shield) all appear in the netlist as individually unconnected ... while the LAN1_RX+/-, LAN1_TX+/- global labels used elsewhere resolve to single-node nets containing only U5 pins. In this netlist export, the Ethernet jack is not wired to the SKW92A's Ethernet PHY nets. (EthernetAndPower, §3 Open item)
EthernetAndPower sheet: J5 left pins TD+/TCT/TD/RCT/RD+/RD connected to labels LAN1_TX+/LAN1_TX-/LAN1_RX+/LAN1_RX-/LED0/(NC); SkylabModule sheet: LED0 label on U5.31 (P4_LED) and on the Q2 gate node.

anomalies.impact: The Ethernet PHY differential pairs are mis-terminated (signal nets shorted to transformer center taps, RX pair broken) so the LAN port cannot work, and the EPD power-switch control net LED0 is DC-coupled into the RJ45 RX winding, loading/contending the U5.31 GPIO and preventing reliable display-power switching.

anomalies.observed: On the EPD_Driver sheet C1 (input decoupling on the Display_Power_Switch / boost-converter input node, in parallel with C2) is drawn as 0.1 uF / 16 V.
anomalies.expected: The specification's component table lists the intended value for this position as 1 uF / 25 V ('C2 default: 1 µF/25 V | C1/C5/C7/C8/C9/C10 = 1 µF/25 V | Matches default').

evidence.quote: C2 default: 1 µF/25 V | C1/C5/C7/C8/C9/C10 = 1 µF/25 V | Matches default (EPD_Driver vs PDI reference, §4 table)
EPD_Driver sheet: C1 = 0.1uF/16V on the Display_Power_Switch node to GND.

anomalies.impact: The boost-converter input bulk decoupling is reduced ~10x versus the intended design, increasing input ripple and potentially degrading boost-converter stability during EPD refresh.

parsed.summary: The drawing deviates from the intended design mainly at the RJ45 jack J5, whose transformer data pins are mis-wired (differential pairs tied to center taps, RX pair broken, and the LED0/display-power-switch net bridged onto a data pin), contradicting the specification's open item that J5's data pads were unconnected and the LAN1 nets were single-node; a secondary value deviation is C1 on the EPD boost input (0.1 uF/16 V vs the specified 1 uF/25 V).
